newsitem.title: LEBANON: GAMES-Iraq Arab games team stranded at Lebanese border.
newsitem.headline: GAMES-Iraq Arab games team stranded at Lebanese border.

text.p: Iraqi athletes waited at a Lebanese frontier post on Friday after Lebanese officials refused to let them enter the country to compete in the Pan Arab Games.

Delegation leader Assil Tabra said the 97 athletes would wait at the dusty Masnaa post on the Syrian-Lebanese frontier until they received official word from Beirut excluding them from the games or allowing them to compete.

The two-weeks-long Pan Arab Games, which are held every four years, open in Beirut on Saturday. They are one of the first major international events staged in the Lebanese capital since the end of the 1975-90 civil war.
If Iraq competes there will be 20 countries participating.

The Iraqi athletes, who arrived at Masnaa at 8.30 a.m. (0530 GMT) in three buses after crossing Syria in a 20-hour drive from Baghdad, were still awaiting permission to enter Lebanon in mid-afternoon more than eight hours later.
The buses carried large photographs of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein and signs saying "Iraqi delegation to the Arab Games."
The athletes lounged around in blue tracksuits or exercised nearby. They included football, volleyball, boxing and kickboxing teams.
Embarrassed Lebanese officials in Beirut dodged reporters seeking clarification whether the Iraqis would be allowed in.
"Don't tell anyone you talked to me," said an official contacted by Reuters by telephone. "We are not going to say anything about this. Let another department handle it."
"Please talk to someone else. I can't say anything," said another official.
A foreign ministry official said on Wednesday Beirut was under pressure from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to exclude the Iraqis from the games.
The two countries, Gulf War foes of Iraq and among the most generous Arab financiers of Lebanon's postwar reconstruction, threatened to boycott the games if Iraq competed, the official said.
"No visas for the delegation," an immigration officer at Masnaa told a Reuters reporter as the Iraqis waited outside in the sweltering heat.
Iraqi delegation chief Tabra told reporters Iraq had received no notification from Lebanon on whether or not its team could compete in the games.
"We will stay here until we receive a letter from Lebanon saying Iraq is excluded from competing in the games or we are allowed to participate," he said.
"But don't say we are staging a sit-in," he added. "I didn't say that. We are just waiting, and we considered what has happened so far as just bad organisation."

Arab League secretary-general Esmat Abdel-Meguid intervened on Wednesday and Lebanese officials said they were in diplomatic contact with Saudi Arabia and Kuwait in a bid to arrange for a symbolic Iraqi presence at the games.
But there has been no word from Lebanon since then to indicate whether its efforts have been successful.
Tabra said another 63 Iraqi athletes were due to arrive on July 18 and 19, hoping to compete in the games.

He showed reporters an invitation to the games and several confirmations which he said Iraq had received since February from Ahmad Qadri abdel-Meguid, assistant secretary-general of the Arab League for social and cultural affairs.

He also showed what he said were invitations from Lebanese Education Minister Jean Obeid, whose ministry is in charge of sports, and from Zeid Khiami, a director-general at the ministry in charge of organising the games.
